gettingStarted.hubTitle: How to get started with Athene
gettingStarted.hubLead: Pick a guide. Each guide shows the order of master data and apps — from required to useful optional steps.
gettingStarted.completeHint: Prerequisites met — guide still available to open

auftragswesen.title: Order management
auftragswesen.summary: Assets and cost centers first — then work orders. Add employees and work groups if you plan people.
auftragswesen.intro: Order management needs clean master data in the same site. Without an asset and cost center you cannot create a work order.
auftragswesen.tip: Site consistency: an asset’s cost center must match the asset’s site. Responsibles must be work-group leaders; assigned employees must belong to the work group.

buchungskreis.title: Check the site
buchungskreis.body: Every work order, asset, and cost center belongs to a site. Create missing plants under Administration → Sites and mark plant sites.

kostenstellen.title: Create cost centers
kostenstellen.body: Cost centers are required for work orders. Create them in the matching site — they drive cost assignment and appear on the order and asset.

assets.title: Create assets
assets.body: Assets are the technical objects you work on. Assign each asset a cost center in the same site. Use the tree structure for hierarchies.

planung.title: Employees & work groups (for planning)
planung.body:
If you want to plan employees and work groups, create both first:
• Employees in master data
• Work groups with members and leaders

Without a work group you can still create orders, but assignment and responsibility will not work properly.

stammdatenExtra.title: Order types & PCR master data
stammdatenExtra.body: Optional but useful: order types, classifications, plus problems, causes, and actions (PCR). They structure reporting and feedback.

auftraege.title: Create the first work order
auftraege.body: Create the order with asset and cost center. For planning: pick a work group, set responsibles (leaders) and assignments. Add planned start/end and order type.

steuern.title: Control & track
steuern.body: Monitoring for the live overview, Calendar for dates, Transactions for time/material, Message center for subscriptions and alerts.

materialwesen.title: Materials
materialwesen.summary: Warehouse → storage locations → spare parts. Then book material on work orders.
materialwesen.intro: Materials live under warehouse management: stock sits in warehouses and storage locations. Spare parts need stock lines before material booking makes sense.
materialwesen.tip: Keep the order: warehouse first, then storage locations under that warehouse, then spare parts with stock control. Material bookings need order, spare part, warehouse, and storage location.

buchungskreis.title: Prepare the site
buchungskreis.body: Warehouses and spare parts are site-scoped. Use the same site as assets and work orders so material and orders stay aligned.

lager.title: Create warehouses
lager.body: Under Warehouse, create physical or logical warehouses (key, name, site, active).

lagerorte.title: Create storage locations
lagerorte.body: Each storage location belongs to exactly one warehouse. That is how you find parts on the shelf and manage stock in enough detail.

ersatzteile.title: Create spare parts with stock
ersatzteile.body: Create spare parts and maintain stock control per warehouse/storage location (quantity, optional reorder point). Without a stock line you will not see available quantity later.

lieferanten.title: Suppliers (optional)
lieferanten.body: Supplier master data helps with procurement and assignment. Useful once purchasing or replenishment matters.

buchen.title: Book material
buchen.body: Material flows via transactions on the work order (Material reference) or the Transactions app. Stock decreases and consumption is tied to the order.

benutzermanagement.title: User management & sites
benutzermanagement.summary: Sites first, then users with a plant primary site and optional employee link.
benutzermanagement.intro: Users control login and data access. Sites limit what someone can see and edit.
benutzermanagement.tip: A user’s primary site must be a plant (isPlant). A user can link to at most one employee — and only in the same site.

buchungskreise.title: Create sites
buchungskreise.body: Create sites, assign a color, and mark plants. Only plant sites may be used as a user’s primary site.

mitarbeiter.title: Create employees (optional, recommended)
mitarbeiter.body: Employees are the people in maintenance (assignment, shifts, work groups). Create them before you link users to real shop-floor people.

benutzer.title: Create users
benutzer.body: Under Administration → Users: set login name, name, password, and primary site. Optionally link the matching employee.

zugriff.title: Assign additional sites
zugriff.body: Besides the primary site you can grant more sites. Without access, the user cannot see that site’s data.

fachgruppen.title: Link work groups
fachgruppen.body: For order planning, add employees to work groups and mark leaders. Only then responsibility and assignment work cleanly.

parameter.title: Check app parameters
parameter.body: Parameters such as GN-ASC (site selection) control whether users may change the site on master data. Adjust under App parameters if needed.

onboarding.introBody:
I’m your intelligent maintenance software. I help with work orders, assets, and maintenance questions.

You’re looking at the web application right now. It also works on phones — and there is a separate, dedicated mobile app for work in the field.

This is alpha version {{version}} — I’m still in the early days. Some things may feel unfinished; we’ll grow together.

Open me anytime with the star in the sidebar. Let’s take a quick look at the main areas.
onboarding.stammdatenBody:
This is the foundation of your plant: assets, the tree structure, employees, cost centers, classifications, work groups, suppliers, and maintenance plans.

Clean master data powers almost everything — start here when you set up the system.
onboarding.peopleBody:
Employees are the people in maintenance — they get assigned to work orders, appear in the shift planner, and join work groups.

Users are the login accounts for signing in. A user can be linked to exactly one employee. Then Athene knows who you are: assignments, work groups, and personal views line up.

Manage users under Administration; employees live here in master data.
onboarding.auftragswesenBody:
The heart of maintenance: create and edit work orders, plan in the calendar, post transactions, and stay informed in the notification center.

From creation to completion — it all comes together here.
onboarding.monitoringBody:
Monitoring is your central control tool for open and active work orders. Get a real-time overview of status, deadlines, and bottlenecks — and step in where needed.

When you want to know what’s running on the floor, Monitoring is often the best place to start.
onboarding.ersatzteileBody:
Warehouses, storage locations, and spare parts keep material supply under control. Stock, issues, and part masters live under inventory.

You’ll know what’s available when a work order needs material.
onboarding.schichtenBody: Shift definitions and the shift planner organize who is on duty when. Plan weeks, assign employees, and keep coverage visible.
onboarding.finishBody:
One last thing: use the Help button in the header to start a guided tour of the current app.

Help is not available everywhere yet, but it is being rolled out to nearly all apps. Monitoring already has it — try it, or finish this introduction.

helpTour.tableEditBody:
The table shows your work orders at a glance. Select a row and use Edit to open the edit panel — as a dialog or fullscreen, depending on settings. Double-click a row to edit as well.

The table is stateful: column width, order, sorting, and similar layout settings are saved in this browser. When you adjust the view, it comes back the next time you visit — without setting it up again.
helpTour.contextMenuBody: Right-click a row to open the large context menu: edit, status actions, subscribe, ask Athene, and more — without going through the header.
helpTour.statusBody: The status column shows each order’s current state — color-coded. Here’s every status with its color:
helpTour.startStopBody: Use the Start/Stop column to control execution: start, pause, or finish an order. The same actions are also in the right-click menu.
helpTour.referencesBody: References show documents, employee assignments, and the inspection checklist at a glance. The badges open the matching areas in the work order dialog.
helpTour.createBody: Use New to create a work order directly from Monitoring. After saving it appears in the list — often live via the connection.
helpTour.filterBody:
Open Search to use the filter panel: status, asset, work group, dates, and more. Narrow the monitor list to the orders that matter right now.

The quick search on the right also filters the list by free text.
helpTour.presetsBody:
Saved queries remember your filter and search combinations. One click restores your view — ideal for shift changes or recurring checks.

And I, Athene, can help here: ask me when you want to build, refine, or understand a query.
helpTour.liveBody: Monitoring stays connected to the server over WebSockets. New, updated, and deleted orders refresh the table in real time and are briefly highlighted — green for create, blue for update, red for delete — no manual reload.
